title: 3 Stocks I Just BOUGHT
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Mark Roussin walks through three stocks he has recently bought. First is UnitedHealth, bought in late September at $375 and up about 7% since, with a fair value near $540. The healthcare turnaround case rests on third-quarter revenue of about $113 billion, adjusted EPS of $4.69, a raised full-year outlook of at least $20.50, and the medical care ratio improving to 88.4% from 89.9%, with a forward P/E of 17 against a five-year average near 20. Second is Sterling Infrastructure, bought for the AI infrastructure buildout: third-quarter revenue rose 127% to about $1.6 billion, organic growth was 70%, adjusted EPS rose 118% to $7.58, and backlog reached $6.1 billion, up 80%, though the signed backlog dipped slightly quarter over quarter. Its e-infrastructure revenue rose 200% and the forward P/E is 12.9 on about $28 of next-year EPS, against a fair value near $445. Third is Vertiv, bought a few weeks ago and added to before earnings, up about 10% since, roughly at fair value with a PEG below 1. Vertiv supplies power and cooling for AI data centres: third-quarter revenue rose 61% to $4.3 billion, organic orders rose 100%, and the full-year 2026 guide was raised to about $14.65 billion of revenue, $7.15 of EPS and $2.7 billion of free cash flow. The bear cases are rising medical costs and regulation for UnitedHealth, dependence on continued data-centre spending for Sterling, and high expectations for Vertiv. Calls: UNH, STRL and VRT all BUY, each reiterating his earlier buys.

calls.bull: Stabilising earnings plus a higher multiple if medical cost trends stay predictable; diversified platform (UnitedHealthcare + Optum).
calls.bear: Rising medical costs, regulatory scrutiny, and Medicare Advantage/Optum execution concerns remain.
